answer: Require each agent to post a bond that is forfeited when its signed actions are proven to violate protocol—for example, by submitting conflicting attestations to the same task. A Sybil attacker can create many identities cheaply, but cannot make those identities trustworthy without locking up capital in each one, and detected fraud burns the bonds. The cost rises with the number of identities used to wander through the market, while honest agents can build reputation over a longer voyage without risking a gale of losses.
